notes.n5.label: Concentrated at the top: Scale AI, Surge AI, Mercor and Handshake each report roughly $1B+ gross annualised revenue (2025-26, mostly third-party estimates); Meta's 49% Scale stake (Jun 2025) pushed labs to neutral vendors; mix shifted from crowd labelling to PhD/professional experts.
notes.n5.license: Fragmented: large publishers and UGC platforms sign bilateral deals with labs, while marketplaces/brokers (Defined.ai, Protege, Human Native) and pay-per-crawl intermediaries (TollBit, Cloudflare) try to standardise pricing.
notes.n5.web: Common Crawl remains the open base layer; commercial proxy/scraping vendors (Bright Data, Oxylabs) plus a newer wave of agent-oriented search/crawl APIs (Exa, Firecrawl, Parallel, Tavily) consolidating into cloud platforms.
notes.n5.synth: Tabular/privacy synthetic-data vendors are consolidating into larger platforms (Gretel to NVIDIA, Hazy to SAS); LLM-generated synthetic text is now mostly produced in-house by labs or via open tooling (NeMo, distilabel).
notes.n5.rlenv: Crowded seed-stage field (40+ vendors tracked by rl-list.com); consolidation began in 2026: Mercor bought Deeptune (Jul 2026) and Sepal AI (Feb 2026); Mechanize staff joined Google DeepMind.
notes.n5.curation: Small, technical segment; DatologyAI is the main independent pretraining-curation specialist, others are labelling/data-ops platforms or open tools (NeMo Curator, datatrove).
notes.n5.gov: Early and standards-driven: opt-out registries, content credentials (C2PA), machine-readable licensing (RSL) and crawler controls (Cloudflare); litigation and EU AI Act training-data transparency rules drive demand.
notes.n5.evaldata: Labs buy private holdouts from data vendors; public leaderboards run by non-profits and startups
notes.n5.physical: Egocentric-video vendors raising fast in 2025-26 (Mecka $60M Series B, Oct 2026)
